text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Former interior minister Janis Adamsons has officially announced his withdrawal from the Latvia's Way faction. He said the reason he was quitting was that he cannot support the government of Andris Shkele, which defends the interests of big business and neglects those of simple people.

- Latvian Defence Minister Andrej Krastinsh quoted U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry as saying the Baltic States will not be admitted to NATO in the first round because they cannot guarantee the security of other alliance members. Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs believes Latvia will continue preparations to join NATO as noone has so far officially announced which countries will be admitted to NATO first.

- The management of the holding company MONO admits the murder of vice-president Valery Machugin could have been caused by the company's plans to cooperate with the supermarket, Europe Center. One of its founders, Igor Conda, was killed in mid-August.
- About 15,000 school-age children in Latvia are not attending school.
- The Second European Congress of Archaeologists opens in Riga.
- The foreign ministry decided to recall Latvia's ambassador in Kiev, Peteris Simpson, to intensify economic relations between the two countries.

- Meeting with President of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe Leena Fisher, President Guntis Ulmanis pledged that Europe's Human Rights Convention will ratified by Latvia before the end of this year.
- While in Strasbourg, Ulmanis was almost 'attacked' by Russian parliamentarians asking him about the situation of Russian-speaking residents in Latvia.
